boundary_assessments.area: Summary Option boundary and complete observed facts
boundary_assessments.assessment: If summaries is Some or scalar_policy is true, SourceProjection records every instruction slot and every direct callee plus the function itself in one traversal. Facts preserve each observed callee as (id, summaries.get(id)), including None rather than filtering it out. A previously absent summary becoming Some changes these actual facts and invalidates the unchanged caller. A policy/context change clears entries. Even the defensive None versus Some(empty map) transition changes fact shape conservatively instead of inventing a proof.

boundary_assessments.area: Shared projection identity and hidden fields
boundary_assessments.assessment: Entry retains Option<Arc<SourceProjection>> and the exact old immutable function. Reuse of projection requires current blocks.ptr_eq(old blocks); safe COW mutations allocate privately and old strong ownership prevents ABA. Projection depends only on block instructions, so changing unrelated local/value fields does not require rebuilding it, while the later actual lower hit still requires exhaustive same_input, current summary facts and collection status. When separately rebuilt slots compare equal, observed IDs are necessarily the same set of those slots plus current function ID; context binds that ID, so source_identity may safely ignore redundant observed-list equality.

Changed raw inputs still run original lower() and its meter. A successful machine output equal to the prior result can retain output identity as before. Removing an unused source scan does not remove current Verify/LIR binding, lowering eligibility, ABI checks, native preflight/object integrity or acceptance-budget debits. Warm lowering still replays recorded original meter cost and keeps original failure behavior. Projection caching and its counters confer no verification authority.
